airport.name: General Leobardo C. Ruiz International Airport

summary: General Leobardo C. Ruiz International Airport (ZCL) serves the historic colonial city of Zacatecas in north-central Mexico, named after a notable Mexican military figure. The airport acts as a key gateway for visitors traveling to the UNESCO World Heritage-listed city center, famous for its silver mining heritage, pink stone architecture, and the iconic Cerro de la Bufa. Situated on a high plateau at roughly 2,440 meters (8,000 feet) above sea level, it handles a mix of domestic and limited international flights.
faqs:
Q: How far is the airport from Zacatecas city center?
A: The airport is located approximately 20 km (12 miles) southeast of the historic center, with a typical drive time of 25-35 minutes depending on traffic.

Q: Which airlines operate at ZCL?
A: The airport is served primarily by Mexican carriers including Aeroméxico, Volaris, and Viva Aerobus, offering flights to Mexico City, Tijuana, Guadalajara, and select U.S. destinations.

Q: Does the airport have international flights?
A: Yes, it offers a small number of seasonal and scheduled international services, mainly to cities in the United States, through U.S. and Mexican carriers.

Q: Is there a high-altitude consideration when flying here?
A: Yes, Zacatecas sits at about 2,440 meters elevation. Travelers unaccustomed to altitude should hydrate well and allow time to acclimatize upon arrival.
transport_tips: Authorized taxi services are available outside the terminal and offer fixed rates to the city center; confirm the price before boarding. Ride-sharing apps have limited availability in the region, so pre-booking a shuttle or taxi is recommended. Rental car agencies operate at the terminal and can be useful for exploring the broader Zacatecas state independently.
